# watchpoint_usage_anomaly_alert (Resource)

Usage anomaly alerts, which notify the tenant's billing recipients when a metered product's run rate rises above that tenant's own trailing baseline. The relative counterpart to `watchpoint_usage_budget`, which alerts on an absolute spend threshold. A per-tenant singleton covering every metered product: declare it at most once. Destroying it turns the alerts off.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Alert when a metered product's run rate rises well above this tenant's own
# trailing baseline. The relative counterpart to a usage budget's absolute
# threshold; the two are orthogonal and most tenants want both.
resource "watchpoint_usage_anomaly_alert" "example" {
  is_enabled  = true
  sensitivity = 3.0
}

resource "watchpoint_usage_budget" "overage_warning" {
  name            = "Warn at $50 overage"
  threshold_cents = 5000
  mode            = "forecast"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `is_enabled` (Boolean) Whether anomaly alerts are evaluated. Defaults to `true`, since declaring the resource is the opt-in. The platform default for a tenant that has never configured it is off.
- `sensitivity` (Number) Standard deviations above the tenant's own baseline before a run rate counts as a spike, between `1.5` and `6.0`. LOWER is more sensitive: `1.5` alerts on modest rises and is noisier, `6.0` alerts only on a dramatic one. Defaults to `3.0`, roughly a once-in-a-few-hundred-hours reading for a well-behaved series.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Tenant ID, which is what this per-tenant setting is keyed on.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Per-tenant singleton, so the import ID is the tenant ID.
terraform import watchpoint_usage_anomaly_alert.example tnt_001
```
